content:
# App Icon Minimalist

Create app icons using a simple, practical approach for non-designers. Get to "good enough" quickly without spending hours in design software.

## Use When

- User needs an app icon but isn't a designer
- Design software feels overwhelming
- User wants to ship quickly without perfecting the icon
- Building a prototype or MVP
- The icon is blocking app launch

## The 3-Step Method

### Step 1: Abstract Core Function into Symbol

Think about what the app **does** at its most essential level, then translate to a simple visual element.

| App Type          | Core Function       | Symbol Ideas                          |
| ----------------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| Communication     | Messaging           | Chat bubble, envelope, speech marks   |
| Task/Productivity | Getting things done | Checkmark, checkbox, clipboard        |
| Media             | Playing content     | Play triangle, music note, film strip |
| Finance           | Money management    | Coin, wallet, chart line              |
| Navigation        | Getting places      | Pin, compass, arrow                   |
| Health            | Body/wellness       | Heart, pulse line, leaf               |
| Social            | Connecting          | People icon, network dots             |
| Tools             | Utility             | Wrench, hammer, gear                  |
| Shopping          | Buying              | Bag, cart, tag                        |
| Learning          | Knowledge           | Book, lightbulb, mortarboard          |

**Tips**: Start with one core function, avoid combining concepts, think in shapes not illustrations.

### Step 2: Place in Frame, Adjust Until "Not Ugly"

**Canvas**: iOS (square with rounded corners), Android (square with rounded corners, safe zone ~66%), Web (square is most versatile)

**Layout**: Center symbol, give breathing room, keep large enough for 64px recognition

**Color**: 1-2 colors from app palette, high contrast, avoid gradients initially

**"Not Ugly" Checklist**:

- [ ] Symbol centered
- [ ] Padding around symbol
- [ ] Colors have contrast
- [ ] Reads clearly at 64px
- [ ] Nothing misaligned

### Step 3: Iterate Later (Optional)

Ship the "good enough" version. Refine when app has users, you have time, or you're bored.

## Platform Specs

| Platform | Base Size   | Safe Area   | Export Formats        |
| -------- | ----------- | ----------- | --------------------- |
| iOS      | 1024x1024px | ~80% center | PNG (all sizes)       |
| Android  | 512x512px   | ~66% center | PNG + adaptive layers |
| Web/PWA  | 512x512px   | ~90% center | PNG, ICO, WebP        |

## Response Format

```
1. Core function: [what the app does]
2. Suggested symbol: [simple shape/concept]
3. Color suggestions: [hex codes if available]
4. Layout: [positioning and sizing guidance]
5. Quick preview description: [what it will look like]

Next steps:
- Export sizes for [platform]
- Test on device
- (Optional) Iterate later
```

## Key Principles

- Get to **done**, not perfect
- Flat design makes simple symbols look professional
- Users care more about what your app does than a perfect icon
- "Boring but clear" beats "creative but confusing"

# Design System Browser

Browse 11 curated design themes with complete color palettes, typography, and visual effects.

## Design Systems

| Name        | Style                | Accent         |
| ----------- | -------------------- | -------------- |
| Bauhaus     | Minimalist, Bold     | Red #D02020    |
| Beam        | Clean, Modern        | Orange #ffaa40 |
| Hand-draw   | Handwritten, Playful | Red #ff6b6b    |
| Kinetic     | Edgy, Bold           | Yellow #DFE104 |
| Luxury      | Elegant, Premium     | Gold #D4AF37   |
| Motion      | Smooth, Fluid        | Blue #3b82f6   |
| Neumorphism | Soft, 3D             | Orange #FF8800 |
| Newsprint   | Editorial, Classic   | Red #CC0000    |
| Playful     | Colorful, Fun        | Purple #8B5CF6 |
| Uber        | Professional         | Blue #276EF1   |
| Win98       | Retro, Nostalgic     | Blue #0000FF   |

## When to Use

- List, browse, or view available design systems
- Get colors, color palettes, themes, design tokens, or style configurations
- Generate CSS variables or Tailwind config from a design system
- Create globals.css or theme file using a specific design system
- Compare design systems or view their screenshots
- Query "what colors", "what theme", "what styling" for a design system

**Do NOT use for:** Creating new design systems, modifying existing system data, generating UI components (only provides tokens/config), or general CSS questions unrelated to these design systems.

## Usage Examples

```
# List all systems
"Show me all design systems"

# Get colors/theme
"What colors does Bauhaus use?"
"Show me the Luxury theme"

# Generate CSS
"Generate CSS variables for Kinetic"
"Create a globals.css using Playful design system"

# Generate Tailwind config
"Create a tailwind config for Uber"
```

## Data Source

```
/Users/someone/.claude/skills/design-system/system.json
```

## Screenshots

```
/Users/someone/.claude/skills/design-system/screenshots/[Name].png
```

content:
# Editorial Card Screenshot

## Overview

Turn source text into a compact, high-contrast HTML information card that follows the user's editorial prompt, then render a screenshot in one of the supported aspect ratios.

Always preserve three output stages unless the user explicitly asks to skip one:

1. Write one sentence judging the information density as high, medium, or low.
2. Output the complete HTML with embedded CSS.
3. Self-check that body text remains readable on mobile.

## Workflow

### 1. Analyze Content Density

Choose layout strategy from the content itself:

- Use "big-character" composition when content is sparse and a single phrase, number, or hook can carry the page.
- Use a two-column or three-column editorial grid when content is dense and needs stronger hierarchy.
- Use oversized numbers, heavy rules, tinted blocks, and pull-quote scale to avoid dead space.
- Do not force dense content into evenly weighted tiles. Build primary blocks, secondary blocks, and lighter supporting blocks.
- Match structure to content type:
  - Ranking / recommendation content: allow asymmetric hero + structured list.
  - Tutorial / analysis / interpretation content: group into overview, core judgment, interpretation, boundary, and conclusion.

Before compressing content, first change the layout skeleton.

- Ratio changes should primarily change reading path, hierarchy, and module arrangement.
- Do not treat ratio changes as a reason to delete content by default.
- Only compress, group, or summarize when the current ratio cannot hold the content clearly after layout has already been restructured.

### 2. Apply the Stored Editorial Rules

Use these defaults unless the user overrides them:

- Import Google Fonts:
  ```html
  <link
    href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Noto+Serif+SC:wght@700;900&family=Noto+Sans+SC:wght@400;500;700&family=Oswald:wght@500;700&family=Inter:wght@400;600;700&display=swap"
    rel="stylesheet"
  />
  ```
- Keep body text at `18px` to `20px` on a 900px-wide composition.
- Keep meta/tag text at `13px` minimum.
- Use compact spacing: container padding `40px` to `50px`, component gaps `30px` to `40px`, line-height `1.5` to `1.6`.
- Add visual weight with `4px` to `6px` accent rules, subtle gray planes, and `4%` noise overlays.
- Favor `#f5f3ed` or similar warm-paper backgrounds unless the user supplies another palette.
- Preserve breathing room. Do not shrink outer margins so much that the card loses composure.
- For title zones, prefer larger line-height and clearer separation from subtitle / summary blocks.
- In dense right-side modules, reduce font weight slightly so the page stays clear without feeling heavy.
- Use stronger internal structure inside blocks: subheads, bullets, numbered lines, compare rows, or secondary labels.
- Avoid equal-weight boxes when the card is dense. At least one module should feel visually heavier than the others.

### 3. Choose the Right Layout Skeleton

Pick ratio-specific structure before writing final copy.

#### `4:3`

- Best for full analytical spread or ranked lists.
- Prefer: hero + summary band + dense two-column list + stronger footer.
- Use one main judgment block before the list so the page does not become a flat wall of 10 equal items.

#### `3:4`

- Keep the same information ambition, but change the reading path.
- Prefer: title band + insight row + mixed large/small body modules.
- Use mixed scales: one heavy primary block, one or two medium blocks, and smaller support blocks.
- Do not let the whole portrait card collapse into a long single column.

#### `1:1`

- Best for ability map, grouped comparison, or balanced editorial overview.
- Prefer: strong hero + one heavier quadrant + three supporting quadrants + dense footer strip.
- Square layouts should feel centered and modular, not evenly tiled.

#### Wide covers (`3:1`, `5:2`, `2.35:1`)

- Reduce paragraph length aggressively.
- Use fewer but larger blocks, stronger headlines, and short support lines.

### 4. Build HTML for Rendering

When HTML will be screenshotted, design the page as a fixed-size canvas instead of a responsive webpage:

- Match the exact pixel dimensions of the selected ratio preset from `references/ratios.md`.
- Treat the card as a design board with explicit `width` and `height`, not as a fluid `100vw / 100vh` layout.
- Remove browser-default margins with `html, body { margin: 0; }`.
- Make the card itself fill the screenshot viewport exactly.
- Avoid interactions, sticky headers, or long scrolling sections.
- Use fixed pixel wrappers, for example:

  ```css
  .frame {
    width: 2000px;
    height: 1500px;
  }

  .card {
    width: 100%;
    height: 100%;
    padding: 48px;
    background: #f5f3ed;
  }
  ```

Do not rely on `100vw`, `100vh`, or responsive container widths as the primary design size for screenshot output.

If the user asks only for HTML, still make the layout screenshot-ready.

Use these structural heuristics when composing the card:

- Fill the proportion intentionally. Rebalance layout according to width / height instead of scaling one static template.
- In `4:3` landscape, asymmetric left-right layouts often work best for dense analytical content.
- In `3:4` portrait, use portrait-friendly mixed grids rather than a single narrow column.
- Keep title, subtitle, summary, and modules separated by explicit rows or bands so they do not collide.
- If using numbered modules, keep numbers visually weak enough that they never collide with titles.
- If a section becomes visually monotonous, introduce contrast through hierarchy changes rather than decorative clutter.
- Let big modules carry richer copy than small modules. Do not give every block the same amount of text.

### 5. Capture the Screenshot

Use the bundled shell script when the user wants a PNG output:

```bash
./scripts/capture_card.sh input.html output.png 3:4
```

Supported ratios and render sizes live in [references/ratios.md](references/ratios.md).

The rendering helper requires a local Chrome or Chromium binary.
It first respects `CHROME_BIN` when set, then falls back to common binary names and a macOS Chrome app path.

Before running the script:

- Save the generated HTML to a local file.
- Ensure the page is self-contained except for fonts.
- If you keep the default font imports, rendering will request Google Fonts over the network.
- Ensure the HTML uses a fixed-size design canvas that matches the chosen ratio preset.
- Ensure the viewport composition already matches the requested ratio.

### 6. Ratio Policy

Accept only these ratio presets:

- `3:4`
- `4:3`
- `1:1`
- `16:9`
- `9:16`
- `2.35:1`
- `3:1`
- `5:2`

If the user gives a ratio outside this set, ask them to map it to the nearest supported preset rather than inventing a new one.

## Output Contract

When responding to a card-generation request:

- Start with exactly one sentence describing information density.
- Then output complete HTML in one code block.
- If the user also requested an image, state the ratio used and the screenshot command after the HTML.
- Keep prose short; the HTML is the deliverable.

## Resources

### `references/ratios.md`

Open this when you need the exact preset names or capture dimensions.

### `references/editorial-card-prompt.md`

Use this as the canonical prompt spec when the user wants the latest validated editorial-card behavior.

### `scripts/capture_card.sh`

Run this to capture a PNG from a local HTML file using a supported ratio preset.
It requires a local Chrome or Chromium binary or an explicit `CHROME_BIN` override.

### `assets/card-template.html`

Use this as a starting shell when you want a minimal ratio-ready HTML canvas before filling in real content.

## Failure Checks

Before finalizing HTML or PNG, explicitly reject the result if any of these happen:

- The title overlaps, visually collides with, or blocks summary/body content.
- The title becomes a narrow vertical strip when more horizontal width is available.
- Dense cards are split into too many equal-weight boxes.
- Large blocks contain too little copy and read like empty containers.
- The canvas shows large areas of dead space that could be filled by stronger hierarchy, richer block content, or a heavier main module.
- The PNG feels meaningfully emptier than the HTML layout intent.

## When to Use This Skill Use this skill when the user asks to: - Create an infographic, information chart, or visualization - Visualize data, processes, timelines, or comparisons - Transform text content into visual formats - Create diagrams, flowcharts, or structured visual content - Generate charts, lists, or hierarchical trees from information **Trigger phrases:** "create infographic", "make a visual", "data visualization", "flow chart", "timeline", "comparison chart", "process diagram" --- ## What This Skill Does This skill generates publication-ready infographic HTML files using [AntV Infographic](https://infographic.antv.vision/). It: 1. Analyzes user content to extract structure (title, description, items, relationships) 2. Selects the appropriate template based on content type 3. Generates AntV Infographic Syntax (a DSL for describing infographics) 4. Creates a standalone HTML file that renders the infographic 5. Enables SVG export for sharing and editing --- ## Inputs | Input | Description | Required | | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | -------- | | Content text | The information to visualize | Yes | | Content language | Language of user's input (affects output text) | Detected | | Template preference | Specific template name, if known | Optional | **Content can include:** - Sequential data (timelines, roadmaps, steps) - Comparison data (pros/cons, A/B analysis) - Hierarchical data (tree structures, org charts) - Statistical data (charts, graphs) - Lists (bullet points, key takeaways) --- ## Outputs | Output | Description | | ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | | AntV Infographic Syntax | DSL code describing the infographic structure | | HTML file | Standalone file at `-infographic.html` that renders in browser | | SVG export | Downloadable SVG from the HTML viewer | --- ## Quick Reference: Template Selection | Content Type | Use Template Series | Examples | | --------------------- | ------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | | Sequential/Process | `sequence-*` | Timelines, roadmaps, steps | | Comparisons (2 items) | `compare-binary-*` | Pros/cons, A/B analysis | | SWOT Analysis | `compare-swot` | Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, Threats | | Hierarchies | `hierarchy-tree-*` | Org charts, tree structures | | Data Charts | `chart-*` | Bar, line, pie, word cloud | | Lists | `list-*` | Bullet points, key items | | Grids | `list-grid-*` | Badge cards, compact grids | | Quadrants | `quadrant-*` | Four-quadrant analysis | | Relationships | `relation-circle-*` | Circular relationships | --- ## Syntax Reference ### Basic Structure ``` infographic <template-name> data title <title text> desc <description text> items - label <item label> value <number> desc <item description> icon <collection/icon-name> theme palette <color1> <color2> <color3> ``` ### Key Rules 1. **First line**: `infographic <template-name>` (must match available templates) 2. **Indentation**: 2 spaces for nested blocks 3. **Arrays**: Use `-` prefix for array items 4. **Icons**: Format as `<collection>/<name>` (e.g., `mdi/rocket-launch`) 5. **Language**: Match user's input language in output text 6. **Comparison templates**: Create exactly 2 root nodes with children ### TypeScript Interface ```ts interface Data { title?: string; desc?: string; items: ItemDatum[]; } interface ItemDatum { icon?: string; label?: string; desc?: string; value?: number; illus?: string; children?: ItemDatum[]; } ``` --- ## Icon & Illustration Resources ### Icons (Iconify) Format: `<collection>/<icon-name>` | Collection | Prefix | Example | | --------------- | ------------ | ------------------- | | Material Design | `mdi/` | `mdi/rocket-launch` | | Font Awesome | `fa/` | `fa/arrow-right` | | Bootstrap Icons | `bi/` | `bi/check-circle` | | Heroicons | `heroicons/` | `heroicons/cog` | Browse: https://icon-sets.iconify.design/ ### Common Icons by Category - **Tech**: `mdi/code-tags`, `mdi/database`, `mdi/api`, `mdi/cloud`, `mdi/brain` - **Business**: `mdi/chart-line`, `mdi/briefcase`, `mdi/currency-usd`, `mdi/trending-up` - **Process**: `mdi/check-circle`, `mdi/arrow-right`, `mdi/cog`, `mdi/progress-clock` - **People**: `mdi/account`, `mdi/account-group`, `mdi/shield-account` ### Illustrations (unDraw) Format: Use filename without `.svg` (e.g., `coding`, `team-work`) Browse: https://undraw.co/illustrations/ | Category | Examples | | -------- | ---------------------------------------------- | | Tech | `coding`, `programmer`, `server`, `cloud-sync` | | Business | `business-plan`, `team-work`, `analytics` | | Abstract | `abstract`, `building-blocks`, `connection` | **Note**: Use `illus` field for illustrations, `icon` field for icons. Not all templates support both. --- ## Theme Customization ### Dark Theme ``` theme dark palette - #61DDAA - #F6BD16 - #F08BB4 ``` ### Hand-drawn Style ``` theme stylize rough base text font-family 851tegakizatsu ``` ### Gradient Fill ``` theme stylize linear-gradient ``` --- ## Available Templates ### Sequence Templates (Sequential/Process) - `sequence-timeline-simple` - Simple timeline - `sequence-timeline-rounded-rect-node` - Timeline with rounded nodes - `sequence-timeline-simple-illus` - Timeline with illustrations - `sequence-roadmap-vertical-simple` - Vertical roadmap - `sequence-roadmap-vertical-plain-text` - Plain text roadmap - `sequence-zigzag-steps-underline-text` - Zigzag steps - `sequence-zigzag-pucks-3d-simple` - 3D zigzag - `sequence-stairs-front-compact-card` - Staircase with cards - `sequence-stairs-front-pill-badge` - Staircase with badges - `sequence-snake-steps-compact-card` - Snake steps compact - `sequence-snake-steps-simple` - Snake steps simple - `sequence-circular-simple` - Circular progression - `sequence-pyramid-simple` - Pyramid diagram - `sequence-color-snake-steps-horizontal-icon-line` - Color snake - `sequence-ascending-stairs-3d-underline-text` - 3D ascending stairs - `sequence-cylinders-3d-simple` - 3D cylinders - `sequence-mountain-underline-text` - Mountain progression - `sequence-filter-mesh-simple` - Filter mesh - `sequence-horizontal-zigzag-simple-illus` - Zigzag with illustrations - `sequence-horizontal-zigzag-underline-text` - Zigzag underline - `sequence-ascending-steps` - Ascending steps ### Compare Templates (Comparisons) - `compare-binary-horizontal-simple-fold` - Binary comparison fold - `compare-binary-horizontal-badge-card-arrow` - Binary with badges - `compare-binary-horizontal-underline-text-vs` - Binary with VS - `compare-hierarchy-left-right-circle-node-pill-badge` - Hierarchy comparison - `compare-swot` - SWOT analysis ### Hierarchy Templates (Tree Structures) - `hierarchy-tree-tech-style-capsule-item` - Tech-style tree - `hierarchy-tree-curved-line-rounded-rect-node` - Curved line tree - `hierarchy-tree-tech-style-badge-card` - Tree with badge cards ### Chart Templates (Data Visualization) - `chart-column-simple` - Column chart - `chart-bar-plain-text` - Bar chart - `chart-line-plain-text` - Line chart - `chart-pie-plain-text` - Pie chart - `chart-pie-compact-card` - Pie chart with cards - `chart-pie-donut-plain-text` - Donut chart - `chart-pie-donut-pill-badge` - Donut with badges - `chart-wordcloud` - Word cloud ### List Templates (Lists/Grids) - `list-grid-badge-card` - Grid with badge cards - `list-grid-candy-card-lite` - Grid with candy cards - `list-grid-ribbon-card` - Grid with ribbon cards - `list-row-horizontal-icon-arrow` - Horizontal row with icons - `list-row-simple-illus` - Horizontal row with illustrations - `list-column-vertical-icon-arrow` - Vertical column with icons - `list-column-simple-vertical-arrow` - Simple vertical arrows - `list-column-done-list` - Done list (checkboxes) - `list-sector-plain-text` - Sector list ### Quadrant Templates - `quadrant-quarter-simple-card` - Four quadrants with cards - `quadrant-quarter-circular` - Circular quadrants - `quadrant-simple-illus` - Quadrants with illustrations ### Relation Templates - `relation-circle-icon-badge` - Circular relationship with icons - `relation-circle-circular-progress` - Circular progress relation --- ## Creation Process ### Step 1: Understand Requirements Extract from user input: - **Title**: Main heading - **Description**: Subtitle or summary - **Items**: Data points with labels, values, descriptions - **Structure**: Sequential, comparative, hierarchical, or list-based - **Language**: Must match user's input language If unclear, ask: - "What is the main title for this infographic?" - "What type of visualization works best? (timeline, comparison, chart, list)" - "What are the key data points to include?" ### Step 2: Generate AntV Infographic Syntax Create the syntax using the template and data structure. ### Step 3: Create HTML File Use the template below to create a standalone HTML file: ```html <!DOCTYPE html> <html lang="en"> <head> <meta charset="UTF-8" /> <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0" /> <title>{title} - Infographic
``` ### Step 4: Output to User 1. Write HTML file as `-infographic.html` 2. Inform user: "Open `<title>-infographic.html` in a browser to view and export as SVG" 3. Offer adjustments: "If you want to change the template, colors, or content, let me know" --- ## Examples ### Example 1: Timeline (Sequence) **Input:** "Create a timeline of internet technology evolution" **Syntax:** ``` infographic list-row-horizontal-icon-arrow data title Internet Technology Evolution desc From Web 1.0 to AI era, key milestones items - time 1991 label Web 1.0 desc Tim Berners-Lee published the first website icon mdi/web - time 2004 label Web 2.0 desc Social media becomes mainstream icon mdi/account-multiple - time 2007 label Mobile desc iPhone changes the world icon mdi/cellphone - time 2023 label AI Large Model desc ChatGPT ignites generative AI icon mdi/brain ``` ### Example 2: Process with Illustrations **Input:** "Visualize our product development phases" **Syntax:** ``` infographic sequence-horizontal-zigzag-simple-illus data title Product Development Phases desc Key stages in our development process items - label Research desc Understanding user needs illus user-research - label Design desc Creating user experience illus design-thinking - label Development desc Building the product illus coding - label Launch desc Going to market illus launch-day ``` ### Example 3: Comparison **Input:** "Compare Python vs JavaScript for backend development" **Syntax:** ``` infographic compare-binary-horizontal-underline-text-vs data title Backend Development Comparison desc Python vs JavaScript items - label Python desc Mature ecosystem, great for data science icon mdi/language-python children - label Pros desc Django, FastAPI, extensive libraries - label Cons desc Slower execution speed - label JavaScript desc Full-stack, ubiquitous on web icon mdi/language-javascript children - label Pros desc Node.js, async-first, huge community - label Cons desc Callback complexity, fragmentation ``` ### Example 4: Hand-drawn Style with Custom Font **Syntax:** ``` infographic list-row-simple-horizontal-arrow theme stylize rough base text font-family 851tegakizatsu data title Project Steps desc Our development workflow items - label Plan desc Define requirements - label Build desc Develop features - label Test desc Quality assurance - label Deploy desc Release to production ``` --- ## Error Handling ### When User Input is Unclear - Ask: "Could you provide more details about what you'd like to visualize?" - Request: "What type of chart would work best? (timeline, comparison, chart, list)" - Clarify: "What are the key data points or steps to include?" ### When Template Selection Fails - Default to `list-row-horizontal-icon-arrow` for general lists - Use `sequence-timeline-simple` for time-based content - Use `compare-binary-horizontal-simple-fold` for comparisons ### When Icons Fail to Load - The resource loader handles failures gracefully - Console logs indicate which resources failed - Try alternative icon names from the same collection ### Language Handling **CRITICAL**: Always preserve the language of the user's input. If user provides Chinese content, the infographic text must be in Chinese. This includes title, descriptions, labels, and all text fields. --- ## Boundaries ### What This Skill DOES - Generate infographic HTML files using AntV Infographic - Provide template selection guidance - Create properly formatted AntV Infographic Syntax - Handle icon and illustration resources from Iconify and unDraw ### What This Skill Does NOT DO - Edit existing infographics (generate new ones instead) - Create custom graphics outside of AntV templates - Generate animated infographics - Export to formats other than HTML/SVG - Modify the AntV Infographic library itself - Create interactive data visualizations beyond what templates support --- ## Quick Tips 1. **Keep it simple**: Start with basic templates, add styling later 2. **Respect language**: Match user's input language in output 3. **Test in browser**: Always verify HTML renders correctly 4. **Offer iteration**: Ask if user wants template/color changes 5. **Use icons wisely**: Icons improve readability, don't overuse

content:
# OPC 一人企业方法论

> 9 个 Agent Skill 组成的完整方法论，从资源盘点到转化闭环。

## 方法论概览

OPC（One-Person Company）是一套面向独立创作者和个体经营者的**可执行方法论**。它不是理论框架，而是通过 9 个 Agent Skill 组成的完整流程，帮助你把已有能力重新组织成一个轻资产、可验证、可复用的个人业务系统。

## 执行流

```
00 总编排 → 01 资源盘点 → 02 利基定位 → 03 价值主张 → 04 商业模式 → 06 MVP 设计 → 07 转化闭环
```

- **01 → 07 线性顺序执行**：按阶段依次推进
- **08 / 09 条件触发**：在实际运营中按需触发（资产沉淀 / 经营复盘）

## 适用场景

- 想从副业开始搭建一人企业的职场人
- 自由职业者需要系统化业务方法的
- 有能力/经验/资源但不知道如何组织成商业体系的
- 想做 MVP 验证而非大而全产品的创业者

## 安装方式

```bash
# 全部安装
npx skills add https://github.com/easychen/opc-methodology/skills/opc-orchestrator
npx skills add https://github.com/easychen/opc-methodology/skills/opc-resource-audit

```

启动后使用 `/opc-orchestrator` 开始建盘流程。

content:
# Impeccable Design Quality

> Before commands, before detection, Impeccable teaches your AI real design.

## 核心理念

Every AI model learned from the same templates. Without intervention, they all produce the same predictable mistakes. Impeccable names them, detects them, and teaches the AI to avoid them.

## 7 Dimensions of Design Quality

| 维度 | 关注点 |
|------|--------|
| Visual Expression | Scale, rhythm, hierarchy, expression |
| Design Systems | Accessibility, systems, theming |
| Spatial Layout | Layout, spacing, composition |
| Responsive Design | Fluid layouts, touch targets |
| Interaction Design | States, feedback, affordances |
| Motion & Polish | Micro-interactions, transitions |
| Content Quality | Clarity, voice, error messages |

## 18 Commands

### Creation
- `/create` — Generate designed UI from requirements
- `/shape` — Structured discovery interview → design brief
- `/craft` — Brief → full implementation flow

### Evaluation
- `/evaluate` — Review against design principles
- `/audit` — Score 5 dimensions with P0-P3 severity
- `/critique` — Nielsen heuristics + persona review

### Refinement
- `/refine` — Iterative improvement pass
- `/polish` — Final visual refinement
- `/bolder` — Strengthen typographic hierarchy
- `/simplify` — Reduce complexity while keeping intent
- `/distill` — Remove unnecessary elements
- `/typeset` — Fix typography scale and rhythm
- `/layout` — Fix layout & spacing issues

### Production
- `/harden` — Production readiness: edge cases, errors
- `/system` — Align to design system tokens

### Context
- `/teach` — Set project design context (.impeccable.md)
- `/extract` — Extract design context from codebase
- `/impeccable` — Master command: teach/craft/extract modes

## Detection Engine

25 deterministic checks across typography, color, layout, motion, and quality:
- Gradient text detection
- Purple palette identification
- Nested card detection
- Low contrast measurement
- Tiny body text flagging
- Emoji-only node detection
- And 19 more rules...

Supports: HTML, CSS, JSX/TSX, Vue, Svelte, CSS-in-JS
Color formats: oklch, oklab, lch, lab, hex, rgb

## Installation

```bash
# Skills Add (Recommended)
npx skills add pbakaus/impeccable

# CLI Global Install
npm i -g impeccable

# Claude Code Plugin
/plugin marketplace add pbakaus/impeccable
```

## Stay Updated

```bash
npx impeccable skills update
```

# Kami — Professional Document Typesetting

Transform any text into beautifully formatted documents. Kami is a document engine designed for AI agents, providing structured templates, design tokens, and build pipelines for professional output.

## Document Templates (8 types)

| Template | Language | Pages | Use Case |
|----------|----------|-------|----------|
| resume | zh/en | 1-2 | Personal CV with project highlights |
| letter | zh/en | 1 | Formal business correspondence |
| equity-report | zh/en | 2-3 | Investment analysis with charts |
| changelog | zh/en | 2 | Version release notes |
| one-pager | zh/en | 1 | Executive summary / project brief |
| portfolio | zh/en | 2-3 | Work showcase with case studies |
| long-doc | zh/en | 3+ | Comprehensive documentation |
| slides | zh/en | N/A | PPTX presentations via python-pptx |

## Diagram Library (14 types)

Flowchart, Timeline, Architecture, Bar Chart, Line Chart, Donut Chart, Quadrant, State Machine, Swimlane, Tree, Venn, Waterfall, Candlestick, Layer Stack.

## Design System

- **Colors**: Warm parchment canvas (#FDFBF6), ink-blue accent (#1B365D), olive secondary (#504E49)
- **Typography**: Chinese serif (TsangerJinKai02) + English serif (Charter/Newsreader)
- **Spacing**: Tight editorial spacing with baseline grid alignment
- **Output**: Print-optimized CSS with @page rules for PDF generation

## Build Pipeline

```bash
# Build specific target
python scripts/build.py resume

# Verify all targets
python scripts/build.py --verify

# Check for unfilled placeholders
python scripts/build.py --check-placeholders

# Detect orphan text lines
python scripts/build.py --check-orphans
```

## Installation

```bash
git clone https://github.com/tw93/Kami.git
cd Kami
pip install -r requirements.txt  # weasyprint, python-pptx, pymupdf
```

Or install as a skill via CDN:
```
https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/tw93/kami@main/dist/kami.zip
```
